analysis.investment_thesis: Action Construction Equipment is the closest thing in this batch to a Magic Formula candidate — ROCE of 40%, ROE of 28.6%, negligible debt (D/E 0.08), revenue growing at 20% CAGR and net profit at 52.8% CAGR over 9 years. The problem is valuation: with EBIT of INR 506 Cr against an EV of ~INR 10,882 Cr, the earnings yield is only ~4.65%, well below the 12% Magic Formula threshold, meaning the market has already discovered and priced this quality.
key_strengths: ROCE of 40% sustained as scale increases — net profit CAGR of 52.8% over 9 years demonstrates genuine operating leverage
Near-debt-free balance sheet (D/E 0.08, total debt INR 16 Cr) with OCF positive 5/5 years — financial resilience in a cyclical industry
Dominant position in India's crane and material-handling market with exposure to long-duration infra capex cycle
key_risks: Earnings yield of ~4.65% is too low for Magic Formula buy signal — stock must be purchased at a significant discount to be worthwhile
Capex surging (INR 221 Cr in FY25 vs INR 48 Cr in FY22) is compressing FCF — FCF fell to INR 206 Cr despite INR 409 Cr net profit
Construction equipment is highly cyclical — any slowdown in Indian infrastructure spending would materially impact earnings
red_flags: EV/EBITDA of 21.4x and P/E of 25.8x — the market is paying a significant growth premium; any earnings miss would reprice sharply
Rising capex trend reduces FCF conversion: FCF/Net Profit dropped from ~83% (FY23) to ~50% (FY25)
Other income (INR 100 Cr, ~24% of net profit in FY25) is elevated — core operating earnings are somewhat overstated
analysis.detailed_analysis:
ACE scores highest among the eligible (non-financial, non-utility, non-real estate) names in this batch. A ROCE of 40% sustained across a near-decade of growth is exceptional — this is exactly the kind of business Greenblatt's formula is designed to identify. Operating margins expanded from 4.9% (FY16) to 15.2% (FY25) while revenue grew 20%+ annually, evidence of genuine competitive advantage in the Indian crane market.

However, Greenblatt is clear: you need the business to be cheap AND good. At an earnings yield of ~4.65%, ACE is priced for continued outperformance — there is no margin of safety. The Magic Formula works best when great businesses are temporarily unloved. ACE is loved, appropriately so. I would revisit aggressively if the stock corrects to an earnings yield of 8-10% (implying a ~50% price decline), which would push it into genuine Magic Formula territory. At current levels, it is a quality compounder but not a Magic Formula buy.
